human_subjects.evidence: E1 description: 'multimodal, high-resolution critical care dataset ... 50,000 patient admissions from adult ICU, PICU and NICU settings'; keywords include 'critical care', 'electronic health records', 'clinical notes'

governance_restrictions.evidence: E2 regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: 'restricted'; 'Access to all CHoRUS data types is controlled'

datasets_shared_available_for_reuse.evidence: distribution_formats populated (OMOP tables, OHNLP output, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst); third_party_sharing.is_shared: true; controlled access with documented registration path. Per the ambiguity rule, approval-gated access defaults to applicable.

software_tools_produced.evidence: external_resources (E10) references the chorus-ai GitHub organization with 28 repositories (chorus-extract-upload, chorus_waveform, CTP-deid, etc.)

data_collection_identified_and_shared.evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated; datasets-shared condition met

publication_identified_and_shared.evidence: No citation field; external_resources lists a project website, GitHub org, NIH RePORTER grant record, program page and a training-program call — none is a publication reference. existing_uses mentions 'publications' generically without identifying any. Gates Element 10 sub-element 2 only.

issues_detected.description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true (patient-level ICU/PICU/NICU records including minors) but no IRB approval, reviewing committee identity, or data protection impact assessment is documented. The datasheet itself flags this honestly ('states no IRB approval'), so this is a faithfully-reported source gap rather than a fabrication, but the consistency expectation still fails.
issues_detected.recommendation: Obtain and document IRB/ethics approvals (or the applicable waiver determinations) from the 14 data-acquisition hospitals, with protocol numbers and reviewing institutions.

issues_detected.description: involves_human_subjects=true but informed_consent is entirely absent; at_risk_populations.source_caveats confirms 'they do not describe consent, assent or guardian permission procedures'. For retrospective EHR data a waiver of consent is the likely mechanism, but the datasheet does not state it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the consent basis — most plausibly an IRB-approved waiver of informed consent for retrospective records — including the handling of pediatric/neonatal admissions.

issues_detected.description: No DOI or RRID; id is a self-minted website fragment URI (https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset), not a registrar-backed persistent identifier. For a partially released dataset this materially limits citability and cross-referencing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a DOI (e.g., via DataCite through the hosting platform) and register an RRID for the resource.

issues_detected.description: A 'current released dataset' is described (50,000 admissions, released as of Aug-Sep 2025) yet no version number, version access method, errata, or formal release date exists; distribution_dates.source_caveats concedes 'no initial release date ... is stated'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Assign explicit version numbers to enclave releases and publish a changelog; record the initial release date.

issues_detected.description: License terms describe the access mechanism (signed licensing agreement, .edu email) but not the substantive reuse permissions (publication rights, redistribution, derivative models), so a prospective user cannot determine what reuse is allowed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Summarize the key terms of the data licensing agreement (permitted uses, publication policy, prohibition on re-identification, export restrictions from the enclave).

issues_detected.description: Maintainer email domain 'mgh.havard.edu' is a typo in the source; the datasheet transcribes it exactly and flags it in source_caveats ('appears to contain a typographical error'). Also 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' lacks a URL scheme. Neither is an evaluator-detected fabrication; both are minor.
issues_detected.recommendation: Confirm the correct contact address with the source and normalize the Bridge2AI URL with an https:// scheme.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata or data dictionary; is_tabular=false is semantically correct for a multimodal dataset, and OMOP CDM conformance implies table structure, but users get no column-level guidance for the ~1.6 billion EHR rows.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variable metadata for the OMOP tables used (including the nursing-flowsheet extensions) or link the published per-modality metadata schemas as they are released.

semantic_insights: Exemplary source-conflict handling: source_caveats reconciles the 50,000 (tier-2 site) vs 45,000+ (tier-4 webinar) admission counts by explicit source tiering, and separately flags that NIH RePORTER's '100,000 critically ill patients' and the site's '100,000 patient admissions' use different units and are unreconciled.
Correctly scopes the MIT License to the project's software repositories rather than the controlled-access data ('no dataset-level license slot is asserted') — a distinction many datasheets get wrong.

Deidentification methods are semantically appropriate per modality: OHNLP tokenization for free text (with notes retained locally), DICOM de-identification for imaging (CTP-deid), and transformation approaches limiting re-identification, all reinforced by controlled enclave access.

The absence of a download_url is semantically correct for an enclave model: data are analyzed in the Bridge2AI Clinical Care Cloud and never downloaded, and platform access instructions are fully documented instead.

NIH grant number OT2OD032701 / 1OT2OD032701-01 matches the NIH [Type][Institute][Serial] pattern and is used consistently across description, funders, and external_resources (RePORTER application ID 10472824).
Careful attribution semantics: RePORTER's sole-PI designation (Eric S. Rosenthal) is kept distinct from Leadership Team membership for five other named individuals, with per-creator source_caveats.

Instances are annotated with B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology terms, and modality-level availability (7,642 radiology admissions, ~1,000 de-identified images, EEG in process, tokens-only notes) is quantified in missing_data_documentation.
Temporal claims are internally consistent: award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 brackets the Aug/Sep 2025 status milestones and the Nov 2025 - Jul 2026 training cohort.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB (PhysioNet), EDF+, OHNLP, Persyst; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.evidence: Learning resources pages on chorus4ai.org, Chorus_SOP interactive workflow, chorus-developer web guide, AIM-AHEAD training program (Cohort 2), OHDSI/OMOP workshops and canonical Jupyter notebooks in intended_uses
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive training and documentation ecosystem documented.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.evidence: No related_datasets field
sub_elements.quality_note: No typed relationships to related datasets (e.g., the three sibling Bridge2AI data-generation projects, or MIMIC/eICU as prior critical-care corpora).

strengths: Exceptional source transparency and conflict reconciliation: source_caveats resolves the 50,000-vs-45,000 admission count by explicit source tiering, flags the unreconciled patients-vs-admissions unit mismatch with NIH RePORTER, scopes the MIT license to software rather than data, and even flags a typo in a published contact email rather than silently correcting or propagating it.

Complete technical transparency (Element 8, 5/5): per-modality collection mechanisms, acquisition methods with correct observed-vs-derived provenance flags, a five-step preprocessing pipeline with named repositories (chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, OHNLP, DeGauss, CTP-deid), and a cleaning feedback loop via CHoRUSReports.

Full motivation and funding transparency (Element 7, 5/5) with a format-valid NIH award number (OT2OD032701 / 1OT2OD032701-01) used consistently and cross-referenced to RePORTER, plus careful PI-versus-leadership attribution.
Strong standards interoperability: OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+, OHNLP and Persyst conformance declared, with the OTHER enum value explicitly expanded.

Modality-appropriate privacy engineering documented: text tokenization with local note retention, imaging de-identification, re-identification-limiting transforms, and controlled enclave access, with explicit residual-risk framing.
weaknesses: No persistent identifier: no DOI or RRID, the id is a self-minted website fragment URI, no publisher is asserted, and no citable publication exists — the dataset is hard to cite or cross-reference despite being partially released.

Ethics documentation gaps for a human-subjects dataset that includes minors: no IRB approval numbers or reviewing committee, and no informed-consent or consent-waiver documentation — both honestly flagged as source gaps but still failing the human-subjects consistency expectations.
Version tracking is nearly absent (Element 6, 2/5): no version number, no version access method, no errata or changelog, and no formal release date for a dataset already in use.
No variable-level metadata or data dictionary for ~1.6 billion OMOP rows; per-modality metadata schemas are described as planned rather than linked.

Reuse permissions are opaque: the licensing agreement's substantive terms are not summarized, and no related_datasets relationships situate CHoRUS among sibling Bridge2AI or prior critical-care datasets.
recommendations: Mint a DOI for the released dataset (and consider an RRID), and assert a publisher, so the enclave-hosted resource becomes citable and cross-referenceable.

Document the IRB/ethics approvals or waiver determinations covering the 14 data-acquisition hospitals, including the consent basis (likely a waiver for retrospective records) and its application to PICU/NICU admissions.
Introduce explicit release versioning with a changelog and formal release dates; record how users pin or reference a specific enclave release.
Publish or link variable-level metadata: the OMOP tables and flowsheet extensions in use, and the per-modality metadata schemas as they move from planned to published.
Summarize the substantive terms of the data licensing agreement (permitted uses, publication rights, re-identification prohibition, enclave export policy) in license_and_use_terms.
Add related_datasets entries with typed relationships — at minimum the sequestered holdout's relationship to the main dataset, sibling Bridge2AI datasets, and antecedent critical-care corpora.
